The log covers one week, six ticket entries, four distinct customers and four underlying events. No causes are diagnosed, so it cannot establish a repeated underlying cause.

Among the four customers represented, two—A and B—reported an export problem. The supplied skill prohibits reporting percentages from a small sample, so the compliant answer is **two of four customers**, without converting that count to a percentage.

This is separate from the ticket-entry share: export problems account for three of the six entries (E1–E3). E1 and E2 concern the same customer and event, so they are two occurrences but only one distinct instance. Nothing here establishes the share among all customers of the service.

| Wording group | Supporting entries | Occurrences | Distinct instances | Finding |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| Export failed | E1, E2, E3 | 3 | 2 | Repeated symptom; cause unknown |
| Login failed | E4 | 1 | 1 | Isolated signal; cause unknown |
| Display failed | E5, E6 | 2 | 1 | Isolated signal with repeated entries; cause unknown |

Confidence is high in these descriptive counts because customer and event identities are explicit. There is insufficient evidence for any shared-cause pattern: matching wording does not establish matching causes, and no diagnostic evidence supports or distinguishes them.

A person should check the diagnoses before deciding whether any finding warrants a fix or process change.
